story: Almost all of the top subreddits are moderated by the same people
text: Radicalisation is actually very interesting and I (ashamedly) nearly succumbed to the same thing myself. Empathy is always at the root of deradicalisation, so I always plug her videos when I can. [VIDEO] [LINK]

story: Ask HN: Is Reddit censorship healthy?
text: It looks like Reddit hasn't censored TRP, just put up a warning. Reddit appears to be free software[0], so you can host your own if you're not OK with that. Haven't read what's on TRP, but if you'd like to listen to informed critique and considerations of it, I'd warmly recommend watching ContraPoints[1]. [0]: [LINK] [1]: [VIDEO]

story: For many young South Koreans, dating is too expensive, or too dangerous
text: The "incel" population also manage to be a self fulfilling prophecy. It's a little dramatic, but [VIDEO] explains it well.

> You can't have a happy society where the top 5% of beautiful men are paying people to schedule their calendar of tinder lays while other guys buy thot bathwater, or where the top 5% of women get all the attention and the rest wonder where their prince charming is who's been denied them from all this as they sadly pass 30 alone. This is so reductive of human relationships. You’re basing your entire worldview on what happens on Tinder and Instagram. That’s not the world, not even close. Basically, I suggest that you watch this: [VIDEO]

Ironically, this video focusing on "incels" has a pretty good understanding of the male online dating experience (starting around 17:00): [VIDEO] I agree that the various "red pill" subcultures have done a terrific job of sucking the air out of the room RE conversations about men's dating experience. It's a hard conversation to have with any amount of nuance in 2022.
